newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs roar to higher end ahead of fund buying.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs roar to higher end ahead of fund buying.

text.p: The Seoul bourse roared to a higher close on Thursday as investors actively bought stocks, on speculation that public pension funds would buy heavily before the end of the year, brokers said.
The composite stock index rose to provisionally close 29.58 points, or 4.47 percent, higher to 690.97.
This was the largest index rise seen this year. The finance ministry has urged the three largest public pension funds to invest 300 billion won in the bourse by the end of the year.
Brokers said that the pension funds were not seen entering the market on Thursday, but they were expected to begin buying up to 30 billion won a day from Friday.

"Today the buying was nearly across the board and the energy strong," said Choi Tae-hwan, head of sales at KLB Securities. "Tomorrow I think the buying will narrow down and investors will concentrate on blue chips and shares that either have strong fundamentals or have fallen significantly."

Financial shares, in particular oversold securities stocks, were the prime focus of the shopping spree. Daewoo Securities closed at its upper limit of 12,300 won, up 900 won. SEOULBANK topped the most active list, gaining 270 won to 4,270.
"Today's market rise is definitely short-term, but good news is that the government has shown a strong will to support the market above 660," said Jay Kwon, a broker at Hanwha Securities.
March futures contract also gained, rising 3.30 points to 69.80, while the KOSPI 200 index jumped 3.88 points to 71.39.
